blocking_defects: B-D2 source and subject_recognition, 25.025 to 28.5 s (s5-shot-2 wide, and the s1 pull-back wisp at 2.5 to 5.0 s at the same point). B's world plume at [640,1040] (scale .62, lean .55) rises 43 px left of the plate's near-pumpjack card (x 683 to 1004) and leans right across it. The beam held on the plume ends on the pumpjack cluster, which the round five strips show at 25.5 to 28.0 s. The picture suggests the camera is watching an oil-well fire, which no claim reports. Same kind of defect as A-P1, less prominent because the wide has no flag box.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: From the silent phone strips and the current code. A tower camera's display pans dry land and pulls back to the tower. 16 of 56 cameras are up. Smoke appears in the display and is flagged. An alert card goes to the crew truck and lands on its dash phone. The dash clock marks an estimated window of up to ten minutes. In the display the plume keeps burning and the cameras don't prevent fires. Wide, the beam ends on smoke at an oil pumpjack while a dashed line from the truck stops short of a responder badge. The utility's wildfire lead reports no major fire since launch over the visor calendar. The record stays blank. The plan waits on state approval.
story_review.opening_to_ending: Opens on what the camera sees and ends on the alert landed with the crew, the line to responders open and the plan awaiting approval, but the s5 wide points the beam at a pumpjack.
story_review.weakest_transition: s4-shot-2 to s5-shot-1: from the dash clock in the cab straight back into the lens display with no physical bridge.
